data.body:
## Phase 2 complete — fix pushed as Gerrit change 2000 (NOT closing; awaiting merge)

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2000 — "Order the enrichment queue by soak deadline"

### CORRECTION to the RCA comment above (AC1)
My earlier trend read said the backlog was "not draining, not growing — stuck". Continued
measurement during this session shows that was wrong, and the correction matters:

| time (2026-08-21) | pending |
|---|---|
| 04:20 | 861 |
| 04:35 | 896 |
| 06:50 | 217 |
| 07:10 | **172** |

**AC1 answer: DRAINING.** The backlog was a step change, not accumulation — a bulk enqueue of
1,067 entries on 08-20 spread uniformly across all id deciles — and it is clearing. My "stuck"
reading came from an end-of-day series whose 08-21 bucket was a partial day; the 08-20 entries
carry a 60-minute soak, so they only became eligible later. **Enqueue is not outpacing the
drain.** The batch cap is therefore not implicated, which independently corroborates the
discriminating experiment that isolated the cause to the order key.

Starvation is nevertheless real and unbounded — it is a property of the *ordering*, not of
depth (see the controlled experiment in the RCA: 40 successful enrichments, 0 of 9 late entries
served, across 8 runs). It bites whenever a churn set of >= `overlap_drain_batch` entries sits
low in id order, regardless of how deep the backlog is.

### The fix
`src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py::pending_enrichment` — order candidates by
`(not_before_ns, ticket_id)` instead of by ticket id alone. 24 insertions / 4 deletions in one
function. No new config, no default retuned, no priority class, no scheduler, no new stored
state, no dependency, no change to the gate marker. `not_before_ns` is the field the queue
already stores and already bumps FORWARD on every re-enqueue as a documented debounce
(`queue.py:8-13`); it was used only as a *filter* and discarded as an *order*, so the debounce
deferred an entry against the clock but not against its peers. The ticket-id tiebreaker keeps
the result deterministic, so `os.listdir` order still cannot leak through.

### Test — RED first, held out, and shown to have teeth
`tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_backlog_drains_despite_a_low_sorted_churn_set`

- **Legitimately RED before any fix existed:** "9 of 9 later-sorted entries were never served
  across 8 drain runs" — the intended assertion, not an import or fixture error.
- **Held out:** moved out of the tree (along with every scratch experiment naming the
  counterfactual key) before the fix subagent was launched; the file was declared off-limits and
  the fixer received only the mechanism, the evidence and the frozen contract card. GREEN was
  verified by the orchestrator after the fixer had finished, against an oracle it never saw.
- **Not tautological:** the expected sets are built from ids the test created (`sorted(tids)`),
  never from `pending_enrichment`. The assertion is on **service** — which entries reach a DONE
  tombstone — not on the order the queue returns, so any fair policy satisfies it.
- **No wall-clock assertion** (`scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py`: clean).

**Kill matrix — 3 mutants seeded, 3 killed, 0 survivors:**

| # | mutation | guarded side | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | restore `sorted(...)` on ticket id (re-introduce the exact root cause) | ordering / fairness | **RED** — "9 of 9 later-sorted entries were never served" |
| 2 | delete the `processed >= batch` break in `drain` | per-run batch cap | **RED** — `test_batch_cap`: `assert 8 == 5` |
| 3 | drop sorting entirely (raw `os.listdir` order) | determinism + fairness | **RED** — "2 of 9 later-sorted entries were never served" |

Honest caveat on #3: it died on the *fairness* axis, because unordered service is also unfair.
The **determinism** property itself is not independently pinned by any test, so #3 does not
demonstrate determinism coverage. That gap is dispositioned below.

**Refactoring litmus:** a behaviour-preserving internal rename inside `pending_enrichment`
(`out` -> `candidate_rows`) left the test GREEN. It asserts persisted store state via
`reduce_ticket(...)["done"]`, never a private name or a grep of source.

### Replication of the original report (live store, read-only)
Against the real tracker with the fix applied, the reported harm is gone. `e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2`
— one of the three tickets the report names, and the single oldest-waiting entry in the queue
(soak deadline 01:37 vs 05:51 for the rest) — moves from **rank 175 of 217** under the old key
to **rank 0** under the new one. Under the old key a 5-per-run drain needed ~35 clean runs to
reach it while re-enqueued entries kept re-filling the front ahead of it; it is now first.

### Gates
`make lint` (incl. complexity ratchet `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`), `make typecheck`
(617 files), `check_wall_clock_asserts` clean, and the full unit sweep: **12,102 passed,
44 skipped, 0 failed.**

### Step 7 sweep
- **Axis 1 (construct).** Class: *an automatically-serviced queue whose entries automatically
  re-enter, ordered by identity, consumed as a capped prefix*. Swept every `return sorted(...)`
  in `src/rebar` (25 hits). None is a sibling: they are deterministic-output helpers (read sets,
  manifests, eval specs, fsck reports) with no batch cap and no automatic re-entry.
  `graph/_hierarchy.py:282` was checked specifically and is archive-eligibility, not a serviced
  queue. **Bounded:** the sweep covered `return sorted(...)` and the queue/drain modules; I did
  not audit every list comprehension that happens to be ordered.
- **Axis 2 (parity).** Rule: *selecting queued work for service must not let an entry's identity
  determine its service order.* Channel census — CLI: `rebar enrich --drain|--once` ->
  `cmd_enrich` -> `drain()` (`enrich_drain.py:497`), holds via the shared core. MCP tool: **N/A**
  (no enrich tool; `grep` over `src/rebar/_mcp/` finds none). Library facade: **N/A** (no
  `rebar.*` export). Automated caller: `maybe_drain` (`enrich_drain.py:460`) -> same core, and it
  only takes `bool()` of the list, so it is order-blind. Dual direction: `status()`
  (`enrich_drain.py:188`) counts buckets and performs no selection — **N/A**. Every surface that
  performs the operation calls the one core I fixed. **No MISSING slots.**

### Residual risk & prevention
- **Determinism of the returned order is unpinned by any test** (observed via mutant #3, which
  survived on that axis and died only on fairness). **Accepted** — the tiebreaker makes it true
  by construction and change 2000's comment states the invariant; pinning it would need a
  fixture that controls `os.listdir` order, which is more machinery than the risk warrants.
- **The write-path gate's cost on a backlogged store** — **ticket filed**:
  `4144-75d3-6af1-47d3` (tireless-convenable-canvasback), linked `discovered_from` this bug and
  `relates_to` `958e-f4b3-275c-4154`. It carries the full scaling table and the scope note that
  a marker redesign is a design change, not a drive-by patch.
- **`958e`'s marker tests never exercise a standing non-empty pending set** — all 9 seed a store
  whose pending set becomes empty, which is why the all-or-nothing branch shipped undiscussed.
  **Ticket filed** (same one — it is an explicit AC there).
- **REPO_ROOT pollution failures while running the suite inside the live checkout**
  (`tests/conftest.py:339`, "New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT: ['.rebar/enrich...']").
  **Accepted, not a defect** — root-caused to `.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` created by detached
  drain children that this session's own `rebar` writes spawned in the same checkout. It does
  not reproduce when the test runs alone, and cannot occur in a clean CI checkout with no
  concurrent drain.

### Not closing
Change 2000 is unmerged. Per the project rule, this ticket stays `in_progress` until the change
is `Verified +1`, `LLM-Review +1`, and submitted. `caused_by` -> `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135` is already
recorded; the close must still pass `--caused-by=c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135 --class=plan_defect`
(an omission against that story's own acceptance criterion, not a later regression).
